SMTO-CMP-0016 — The AI's "task finished" message was filled in incorrectly

GUID: 6d4bcdb0-3723-4423-ac6c-1819b0f51182
Slug: completion-invalid-completion-declaration
Domain: CMP · Subsystem: cmp

What happened

  • The AI model's message saying the task is finished had some details in the wrong format. Its proof passed SMTO's checks, so SMTO asked it to fix only the format. Finished work is kept.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Give the task a moment. SMTO normally asks the AI to fix the format, and the task finishes on its own. Only the message format is wrong; the proof of the work already passed SMTO's checks.
  2. If the task shows Partial · resumable, select Resume on the task. SMTO asks the AI to resend the finish message with the same proof, without repeating any work.
  3. If this keeps happening, ask the person who manages SMTO to try a different Main model in Settings › Setup › Model routing. The finish message is written by the AI model, and some models follow the format less reliably.

What success looks like

  • The task shows Completed and its final reply appears under it.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, noting which model the task used. Check whether the earlier action already happened before anything is repeated. Don't restart the task; its finished work doesn't need to run again.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Schema-rejection recovery found a finish_task declaration whose status, evidence and checks validate but whose remaining metadata fails the advertised schema, and returned correction feedback (reason invalid_completion_declaration).

What this means

  • Schema-rejection recovery recognizes a completion declaration that needs correction and emits bounded feedback for the advertised finish_task metadata contract. Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.

Why this can happen

  • Schema-rejection recovery recognizes a completion declaration that needs correction and emits bounded feedback for the advertised finish_task metadata contract.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the specific declaration field/schema error rather than treating it as an execution failure.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the schema error for the rejected finish_task call against the advertised finish_task parameters (recover_schema_rejection in src/agent_runtime/native/recovery.py). The model must resend finish_task with the same cited evidence and corrected metadata; protocol.completion_retry_bound limits attempts, and repeated failures point to a model that does not follow the tool schema (change it under Settings › Setup › Model routing).
  • Correct the completion declaration to the currently advertised schema.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported declaration validates against unchanged retained task evidence.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
